stem: During daily rounds, the nurse notes that a client's central venous catheter no longer has a current clinical indication. Which action is most consistent with central-line infection-prevention guidance?

options.A: Promptly communicate that the catheter is no longer necessary and facilitate removal according to the care plan and facility process
options.B: Leave the catheter in place indefinitely because infection risk does not increase with unnecessary catheter days
options.C: Replace the catheter routinely with a new central line solely to prevent infection, even though central access is no longer needed
options.D: Keep the catheter until discharge because insertion-site care eliminates the infection risk of an unnecessary line

rationale: Central-line infection prevention includes both safe insertion and limiting unnecessary catheter exposure. CDC guidance emphasizes appropriate site selection, maximal sterile barrier precautions and chlorhexidine skin preparation during insertion, and prompt removal of central catheters that are no longer essential. Routine replacement solely to prevent infection is not recommended.
educational_objective: Recognize prompt removal of a no-longer-needed central venous catheter as a key CLABSI-prevention strategy distinct from insertion-bundle elements.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source_document_title: Intravascular Catheter-related Infection Prevention Guidelines — Prevention Strategies and Summary of Recommendations
source_version_date: CDC web update April 12, 2024; current guidance accessed 2026
source_locator: Prevention Strategies: prompt removal of unnecessary central catheters identified during daily rounds; Summary Recommendations: maximal sterile barriers, >0.5% chlorhexidine with alcohol for CVC insertion; do not routinely replace CVCs solely to prevent infection
source_claim_supported: Prompt removal of unnecessary central catheters reduces exposure risk and is part of comprehensive CLABSI prevention; insertion and maintenance measures are distinct components.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — invasive-device infection prevention and safe equipment/device management
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — central-line necessity review
correction_summary: Separated insertion-bundle elements from post-insertion necessity review. Rebuilt the source checklist recall into a daily-rounds decision about prompt removal of an unnecessary central line.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: CDC current intravascular-catheter prevention guidance verified.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Prompt removal, insertion barrier/skin-prep measures and avoidance of routine replacement are source-supported.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; unnecessary catheter days increase avoidable exposure.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; routine CVC replacement solely for infection prevention is not recommended.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; maintenance care does not justify an unnecessary line.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A reduces unnecessary device exposure while respecting facility/provider removal process.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices are management actions for the no-longer-needed line.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked nurse removal authority, emergent access need, routine replacement and insertion-vs-maintenance bundle terminology; no unresolved conflict.
